answer: One concrete mechanism: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because tide only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, nadir is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any terrace approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
